hero: At night in a provincial hospital pediatric ward in Nueva Ecija, a Filipino pediatric nephrologist and a young resident examine an infusion pump and a clear fluid bag beside a crib where a sleeping toddler lies with a grandmother watching anxiously; soft lamp light, concerned but calm mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Non-osmotic ADH plus hypotonic fluid causes hyponatremia and brain swelling.
figures.content: Left: sick child icons (vomiting, pain, pneumonia, surgery) with arrow to pituitary labeled 'ADH on'. Center: kidney with arrow 'keeps free water'. Top: IV bag labeled 'Hypotonic drip' feeding water drops. Right: serum sodium gauge falling to '121 mmol/L', then a brain inside a skull with cells swelling, label 'No room to swell'. Bottom contrast panel: 'Isotonic maintenance: 4% vs 11% hyponatremia (PIMS)'.

figures.teaches: The dengue fluid plan changes with the phase.
figures.content: Horizontal timeline with three colored bands: 'Febrile' (fever line high); 'Critical' (around defervescence, days 3–7, lasting 24–48 hours; vessel icon leaking; hematocrit rising); 'Recovery' (fluid returning to vessels; warning icon 'Overload risk': effusions, high BP). Under each band, one action: 'Replace losses', 'Enough, not more; reassess', 'Reduce or stop'.

card: A fluid bag and infusion pump beside a toddler's crib in a dim hospital ward, no text.
